on_complete.text: Noon. Down on the square Hedda is ringing a handbell, which is not the festival bell, and shouting for everybody to come back to the stage for the evening.

obj/fetch-the-fireworks.text: The storeroom is stacked to the rafters with rockets. Bernt, at your elbow, says 'Oh, good,' in a voice that means he had given up.

barks: Mind the stairs. The stairs do not mind you.
Three goats. Pearl, Barley and the Admiral. The Admiral is the problem.
The cake is resting. Do not slam any doors near the cake.
Six crates of the feast in the bay. Row gently. Crates are shy.
By-law fourteen: the bell rings at dusk. By-law fourteen did not foresee the rope.

on_complete.text: The lighthouse beam sweeps over the square, and every face turns up into it as it passes.
The lighthouse stays dark, so Hedda reads her speech by a lantern Oskar holds up for her, and gets most of it right.
The castle's fireworks fill the whole sky over the town, and keep filling it until the dogs give up barking.
A few rockets go up, one after another, a polite gap between each. The town cheers every one of them, individually.
